p.src: Now Cao Cao raised his sword to kill Zhang Liao, but Xuande seized his arm while Yunchang knelt before him. Xuande said, “A man of such wholehearted loyalty is precisely the kind we ought to retain and employ.” Yunchang said, “I have long known Wenyuan to be a man of loyalty and honor. I pledge my life for him.” Cao Cao tossed down his sword and laughed. “I too know Wenyuan to be loyal and honorable. I was only testing him.” He personally untied Zhang Liao, took off his own robe and clothed him in it, then invited him to the seat of honor. Moved by this treatment, Zhang Liao surrendered. Cao Cao appointed Zhang Liao General of the Household, granted him the rank of Marquis Within the Passes, and sent him to win Zang Ba’s submission. Hearing that Lü Bu was dead and Zhang Liao had surrendered, Zang Ba led his own troops over in submission as well. Cao Cao rewarded him handsomely. Zang Ba also induced Sun Guan, Wu Dun, and Yin Li to surrender; only Chang Xi still refused allegiance. Cao Cao appointed Zang Ba Chancellor of Langya. Sun Guan and the others were likewise promoted and ordered to guard the coastal districts of Qingzhou and Xuzhou. Lü Bu’s wife and daughter were taken by carriage back to the capital, Xu. After lavishly rewarding the three armies, Cao Cao struck camp and began the homeward march. As they passed through Xuzhou, the people burned incense and blocked the road, begging that Governor Liu be left there as provincial governor. Cao Cao said, “Governor Liu’s merits are great. Let him first have audience with the Emperor and receive rank and title; it will not be too late for him to return afterward.” The people bowed their thanks. Cao Cao summoned General of Chariots and Cavalry Che Zhou and placed him temporarily in charge of Xuzhou. When Cao Cao’s army returned to Xuchang, he rewarded all who had served in the campaign and settled Xuande in a residence near the Chancellor’s mansion.

p.src: When the Emperor traced the genealogy, Xuande proved to be his uncle by lineage. The Emperor was overjoyed and invited him into a side hall to observe the courtesies between nephew and uncle. The Emperor thought privately, “Cao Cao has usurped authority, and affairs of state are no longer mine to decide. Now that I have gained such a heroic uncle, I have an ally!” He accordingly appointed Xuande General of the Left and Marquis of Yicheng Village. After being honored at a banquet, Xuande thanked the Emperor for his grace and withdrew from court. From then on, everyone called him the Imperial Uncle Liu.

p.src: When Cao Cao returned to his residence, Xun Yu and the other advisers came in and said, “The Son of Heaven has acknowledged Liu Bei as his uncle. We fear this will not benefit you, my lord.” Cao Cao said, “Since he has been acknowledged as the Imperial Uncle, I shall command him by imperial edict, and he will be still less daring in disobedience. Besides, by keeping him in the capital, Xu, he may nominally be close to the sovereign, but in truth he remains within my grasp. What have I to fear? What concerns me is that Grand Commandant Yang Biao is related to Yuan Shu; if he should aid the two Yuans from within, the harm would be grave. He must be eliminated at once.” He secretly ordered someone to accuse Yang Biao falsely of colluding with Yuan Shu, then had Yang Biao imprisoned and commanded Man Chong to investigate and prosecute him.

p.src: At the time, Kong Rong, Governor of Beihai, was in the capital, Xu. He remonstrated with Cao Cao: “Lord Yang’s family has been renowned for purity and virtue for four generations. How can he be condemned merely because of the Yuan clan?” Cao Cao said, “It is the court’s will.” Kong Rong replied, “If King Cheng ordered the Duke of Shao killed, could the Duke of Zhou claim to know nothing of it?” Left with no alternative, Cao Cao dismissed Yang Biao from office and released him to return home. Zhao Yan, a Gentleman Consultant, was outraged by Cao Cao’s tyranny and submitted a memorial impeaching him for disregarding the Emperor’s will and arbitrarily arresting a high minister. Cao Cao flew into a rage and immediately had Zhao Yan arrested and killed. Thereafter, every official at court trembled with fear. The adviser Cheng Yu said to Cao Cao, “My lord’s power and fame grow daily. Why not seize this moment to undertake the work of a king and hegemon?” Cao Cao replied, “The court still has many loyal pillars of state; I cannot act rashly. I shall ask the Son of Heaven to hold a hunt, so that I may observe how matters stand.”

p.src: Fine horses, celebrated hawks, and swift hounds were selected, and bows and arrows made ready. Cao Cao first assembled troops outside the city, then entered the palace to ask the Son of Heaven to hunt. The Emperor said, “I fear hunting is not a proper pursuit.” Cao Cao replied, “The emperors and kings of old hunted in spring, summer, autumn, and winter, going out to the countryside in every season to display their martial readiness to the realm. Now, when all within the four seas is in turmoil, we should indeed use the hunt to drill the troops.” The Emperor dared not refuse. He immediately mounted his Xiaoyao horse, took his jeweled carved bow and gold-tipped arrows, and rode out of the city in the imperial procession. Xuande, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei each strung a bow and set arrows in his quiver. Wearing breastplates beneath their robes and holding weapons in hand, they led several dozen horsemen after the imperial carriage out of Xuchang. Cao Cao rode his horse Yellow Claw Flying Lightning and led a host of one hundred thousand to hunt with the Son of Heaven at Xutian. The soldiers spread out to form a hunting enclosure more than two hundred li around. Cao Cao rode abreast of the Son of Heaven, scarcely a horse’s head behind him. Behind them rode only Cao Cao’s trusted officers. The civil and military officials attended from far behind; who among them dared approach?

p.src: That day, Emperor Xian galloped to Xutian, where Liu Xuande greeted him respectfully by the roadside. The Emperor said, “Today I wish to see my Imperial Uncle shoot in the hunt.” Xuande obeyed and mounted his horse. Suddenly, a hare was flushed from the grass. Xuande shot, and his arrow struck the hare squarely. The Emperor applauded. After rounding an earthen slope, they suddenly saw a great stag driven out of a thicket. The Emperor loosed three arrows in succession but missed. Turning to Cao Cao, he said, “You shoot it.” Cao Cao asked for the Emperor’s jeweled carved bow and gold-tipped arrow, drew the string fully, and shot. The arrow struck the stag squarely in the back, and it fell in the grass. Seeing the gold-tipped arrow, the assembled ministers and officers assumed the Son of Heaven had made the shot. All leapt with joy, faced the Emperor, and cried, “Long live Your Majesty!” Cao Cao spurred his horse straight forward, placed himself before the Son of Heaven, and received their acclaim. Everyone turned pale.

p.src: Behind Xuande, Yunchang flew into a rage. Raising his silkworm-shaped brows and opening wide his phoenix eyes, he lifted his blade, urged his horse forward, and made to cut Cao Cao down. Seeing this, Xuande hastily shook his hand and signaled with his eyes. When Lord Guan saw his brother’s signal, he dared not move. Xuande leaned toward Cao Cao and offered congratulations: “Your Excellency’s divine marksmanship is rarely equaled in this world!” Cao Cao laughed. “It was merely the Son of Heaven’s boundless good fortune.” He then turned his horse and congratulated the Son of Heaven, but never returned the jeweled carved bow, instead hanging it upon himself.

p.src: When the hunt ended, a banquet was held at Xutian. After the banquet, the imperial procession returned to the capital, Xu. Everyone went separately to rest. Yunchang asked Xuande, “The traitor Cao insults and deceives his sovereign. I meant to kill him and rid the realm of this scourge. Why did you stop me, brother?” Xuande said, “When throwing at a rat, one must beware of breaking the vessel beside it. Cao Cao was only a horse’s head away from the Emperor, with his trusted men crowded all around them. If you had given way to a moment’s anger and acted rashly, and the attempt had failed or the Son of Heaven had been harmed, the guilt would instead have fallen upon us.” Yunchang said, “If we do not kill this traitor today, he is certain to bring disaster later.” Xuande replied, “For now, keep this secret. Do not speak of it lightly.”

p.src: Now Emperor Xian returned to the palace and said tearfully to Empress Fu, “Ever since I ascended the throne, treacherous warlords have arisen on every side. First I suffered the calamity of Dong Zhuo, and afterward the turmoil caused by Li Jue and Guo Si. You and I have endured hardships that ordinary people have never known. Later I gained Cao Cao and believed him to be a minister who would uphold the dynasty; I never imagined he would monopolize the state, manipulate power, and dispense rewards and punishments at will. Whenever I see him, I feel as though thorns were pricking my back. Today at the hunting ground he placed himself before me to receive the acclamations. His insolence has reached its utmost limit! Sooner or later he is certain to harbor some treacherous design, and neither you nor I know where we shall meet our deaths!” Empress Fu said, “All the lords and ministers at court live upon the stipends of Han. Is there truly not one among them who can save the state from calamity?”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, a man suddenly entered from outside and said, “Your Majesty and Your Majesty the Empress, do not grieve; I can recommend a man who can rid the realm of this scourge.” The Emperor looked and saw that it was Fu Wan, father of Empress Fu. Wiping away his tears, the Emperor asked, “My imperial father-in-law, do you too know of the villain Cao Cao’s tyranny?” Fu Wan replied, “Who did not witness the deer hunt at Xutian? But throughout the court, all are either members of Cao Cao’s clan or his retainers. Unless he were a kinsman of the imperial house, who would willingly devote himself to destroying the traitor? This old minister has no authority and cannot carry out the deed. But General of Chariots and Cavalry Dong Cheng, Your Majesty’s imperial uncle, may be entrusted with it.” The Emperor said, “Imperial Uncle Dong has often hastened to the aid of the state; I have long known it myself. He may be summoned within so that we can deliberate on this great affair.” Fu Wan said, “All those around Your Majesty are the villain Cao Cao’s trusted agents. Should the secret leak, the consequences would be dire.” “Then what is to be done?” asked the Emperor. Fu Wan replied, “I have a plan. Your Majesty should have a robe made and take a jade girdle, then secretly bestow them upon Dong Cheng. Sew a secret edict inside the girdle’s lining before giving it to him. Once home, he will discover the edict and can devise plans day and night. Neither gods nor ghosts will know of it.”

p.src: The Emperor approved, and Fu Wan took his leave. The Emperor then composed a secret edict himself, bit open the tip of his finger, and wrote it in blood. He secretly ordered Empress Fu to sew it within the purple brocade lining of the jade girdle, then donned the brocade robe and fastened the girdle upon himself before ordering a palace secretary to summon Dong Cheng. After Dong Cheng had paid his respects, the Emperor said, “Last night the Empress and I spoke of the hardships at the Ba River. Recalling your great service, Imperial Uncle, I specially summoned you to offer my慰問.” Dong Cheng bowed his head to the ground in thanks. The Emperor led him out of the hall to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, then turned into the Gallery of Meritorious Ministers. After burning incense and completing the rites, the Emperor showed Dong Cheng the portraits. In the center hung a portrait of Gaozu, founder of the Han. The Emperor asked, “From what station did our Emperor Gaozu first arise? And how did he found his great enterprise?” Greatly startled, Dong Cheng replied, “Your Majesty is surely jesting with your servant. How could I not know the deeds of our sacred ancestor? Emperor Gao began as a pavilion chief on the Si River. Taking up a three-foot sword, he slew the serpent and raised the standard of righteousness. He swept across the realm, overthrew Qin in three years, destroyed Chu in five, and thus won all under Heaven, establishing a foundation for ten thousand generations.” The Emperor said, “Our ancestor was such a hero, yet his descendants are so feeble. Is that not lamentable?” Then, pointing to the portraits of the two chief ministers on either side, he said, “Are these not Zhang Liang, Marquis of Liu, and Xiao He, Marquis of Zan?” “Indeed they are,” replied Dong Cheng. When Gaozu founded his dynasty and established his great enterprise, he truly depended upon the strength of these two men.” The Emperor looked back and saw that his attendants were some distance away, so he whispered to Dong Cheng, “You too should stand beside me as these two stood beside Gaozu.” Dong Cheng replied, “Your servant has not an inch of merit. How could I be worthy of such a place?” The Emperor said, “I have never for a moment forgotten your service in rescuing me at the western capital, but I have nothing suitable with which to reward you.” Pointing to the robe and girdle he wore, he continued, “You shall wear this robe of mine and fasten this girdle of mine, so that you may always seem to be at my side.” Dong Cheng bowed his head to the ground in thanks. The Emperor removed the robe and girdle and bestowed them upon Dong Cheng, whispering, “When you return home, examine them closely, and do not disappoint my intent.”

p.src: Understanding the hint, Dong Cheng put on the robe and girdle, took leave of the Emperor, and descended from the gallery. Someone had already reported to Cao Cao, “The Emperor and Dong Cheng have gone up to the Gallery of Meritorious Ministers to talk.” Cao Cao immediately entered the court to investigate. Dong Cheng had left the gallery and had just passed through the palace gate when he met Cao Cao coming toward him. With nowhere to hide in time, he could only stand beside the road and salute. Cao Cao asked, “Where have you come from, Imperial Uncle?” Dong Cheng replied, “I was just summoned by the Son of Heaven and presented with this brocade robe and jade girdle.” “Why were they bestowed upon you?” asked Cao Cao. Dong Cheng replied, “His Majesty remembered my former service in rescuing him at the western capital and therefore granted me this reward.” Cao Cao said, “Take off the girdle and let me see it.” Dong Cheng knew that a secret edict must be hidden in the robe or girdle. Fearing Cao Cao would discover it, he hesitated to remove the girdle. Cao Cao shouted at his attendants, “Take it off him at once!” After examining it for some time, Cao Cao laughed and said, “It truly is a fine jade girdle! Now take off the brocade robe and lend it to me for inspection.” Terrified, Dong Cheng dared not disobey. He removed the robe and presented it. Cao Cao lifted it with his own hands and examined it closely against the sunlight. When he had finished, he put it on himself, fastened the jade girdle, and turned to his attendants. “How is the length?” he asked. They all praised how well it suited him. Cao Cao said to Dong Cheng, “What if you were to pass this robe and girdle on to me as a gift, Imperial Uncle?” Dong Cheng pleaded, “They were bestowed by my sovereign, so I dare not give them to another. Allow me to have others made especially to present to you.” Cao Cao said, “Since you have received these garments and girdle, can it be that some scheme lies within them?” Startled, Dong Cheng cried, “How would I dare? If the Prime Minister desires them, then you should keep them.” Cao Cao replied, “These were a gift from your sovereign. Why should I take them from you? I was merely jesting.” He then removed the robe and girdle and returned them to Dong Cheng.

Cao Cao shouted at his attendants, “Take it off him at once!”
After examining it for some time, Cao Cao laughed and said, “It truly is a fine jade girdle!
Now take off the brocade robe and lend it to me for inspection.”
Terrified, Dong Cheng dared not disobey. He removed the robe and presented it.
Cao Cao lifted it with his own hands and examined it closely against the sunlight.
When he had finished, he put it on himself, fastened the jade girdle, and turned to his attendants. “How is the length?” he asked.
They all praised how well it suited him.
Cao Cao said to Dong Cheng, “What if you were to pass this robe and girdle on to me as a gift, Imperial Uncle?”
Dong Cheng pleaded, “They were bestowed by my sovereign, so I dare not give them to another.
Allow me to have others made especially to present to you.”
Cao Cao said, “Since you have received these garments and girdle, can it be that some scheme lies within them?”
Startled, Dong Cheng cried, “How would I dare?
If the Prime Minister desires them, then you should keep them.”
Cao Cao replied, “These were a gift from your sovereign. Why should I take them from you?
I was merely jesting.”
He then removed the robe and girdle and returned them to Dong Cheng.

p.src: Dong Cheng took leave of Cao Cao and returned home. That night, sitting alone in his study, he repeatedly examined the robe with great care but found nothing in it. He thought, “The Son of Heaven bestowed this robe and girdle upon me and commanded me to examine them closely. Surely he did not do so without purpose. Yet why can I find no trace of anything?” He then took up the jade girdle and inspected it. It was exquisitely fashioned of white jade, carved with little dragons winding through flowers; its back was lined with purple silk and neatly stitched, yet there too he found nothing. Still suspicious, Dong Cheng laid it on the table and searched it over and over. After a long while, he grew utterly weary. Just as he was about to rest his head on the desk and sleep, the charred wick of the lamp suddenly fell upon the girdle and set its backing alight. Dong Cheng hastily brushed it away, but a hole had already burned through. Plain silk showed faintly beneath, and traces of blood could dimly be seen. He quickly took a knife, cut the lining open, and discovered a secret edict written in the Son of Heaven’s own hand and blood. The edict read:

p.src: When Dong Cheng finished reading it, tears streamed down his face, and all night he could not sleep. At dawn he rose and returned to the study, where he read the edict over and over, yet could devise no course of action. He laid the edict on the desk and pondered a plan to destroy Cao Cao. Still unable to decide, he leaned upon the desk and lay down. Suddenly, Palace Attendant Wang Zifu arrived. The gatekeeper knew that Wang Zifu and Dong Cheng were close friends and dared not stop him, so Wang Zifu went straight into the study. He saw Dong Cheng slumped over, fast asleep, with plain silk pinned beneath his sleeve and the character “We” faintly exposed. Suspicious, Wang Zifu silently took it up and read it through. Hiding it in his sleeve, he called to Dong Cheng, “How carefree you are, Imperial Uncle! How can you possibly sleep at a time like this?”

p.src: Dong Cheng awoke with a start. Finding the edict gone, he was frightened out of his wits and flailed about in panic. Wang Zifu said, “You intend to kill Lord Cao! I shall denounce you.” Dong Cheng pleaded through his tears, “If you do that, brother, the house of Han is finished!” Wang Zifu replied, “I was only jesting. My ancestors have received stipends from the Han for generations. How could I lack a loyal heart? I wish to lend you my strength so that together we may execute the traitor to the state.” Dong Cheng said, “That you possess such resolve is a great blessing for the state.” Wang Zifu said, “We should enter a secret chamber and sign a covenant of righteousness together, each willing to sacrifice his three clans in order to repay our Han sovereign.” Overjoyed, Dong Cheng took a length of white silk and was first to write and sign his name. Wang Zifu likewise immediately wrote and signed his name. When they had finished, Wang Zifu said, “General Wu Zilan is my closest friend. He may be admitted to our plot.” Dong Cheng replied, “Of all the ministers at court, only Zhong Ji, Commandant of Changshui, and Wu Shuo, Gentleman Consultant, are my trusted confidants. They will surely join us in this undertaking.”

p.src: While they were still discussing the matter, a household servant entered to report that Zhong Ji and Wu Shuo had come to call. Dong Cheng said, “Heaven itself is aiding me!” He told Wang Zifu to hide temporarily behind a screen. Dong Cheng received the two men and led them into his study. Once they were seated and had finished their tea, Zhong Ji said, “Do you too harbor resentment over the imperial hunt at Xutian?” Dong Cheng replied, “Though I resent it, there is nothing I can do.” Wu Shuo said, “I have sworn to kill that traitor; my only regret is that I have no one to aid me!” Zhong Ji said, “If I can rid the realm of this scourge, I shall have no regrets even if I die.” Wang Zifu stepped out from behind the screen and said, “So you two intend to kill Chancellor Cao! I shall denounce you, and Imperial Uncle Dong shall serve as my witness.” Zhong Ji said angrily, “A loyal minister does not fear death. We would sooner die and become ghosts of the Han than live as you do, fawning upon a traitor to the realm!” Dong Cheng laughed and said, “It was precisely to discuss this matter that we wished to see you both. Vice Minister Wang was only jesting.” He then drew the edict from his sleeve and showed it to the two men. When they had read the edict, tears streamed endlessly from their eyes. Dong Cheng then asked them to add their names. Zifu said, “Wait here a moment, gentlemen. I shall go and invite Wu Zilan.”

p.src: Before long, Zifu returned with Zilan. After greeting everyone, Zilan too added his name. Dong Cheng invited them all to drink in the rear hall. Suddenly, word came that Ma Teng, Governor of Xiliang, had arrived to see him. Dong Cheng said, “Tell him merely that I am ill and cannot receive him.” The gatekeeper went back and delivered the message. Ma Teng flew into a rage and said, “Last night, outside the Donghua Gate, I saw him with my own eyes coming out in a brocade robe and jade girdle. Why does he now pretend to be ill? I have not come here without cause. How can he refuse to see me!” The gatekeeper went in and reported Ma Teng’s anger in full. Dong Cheng rose and said, “Gentlemen, wait here a moment while I step outside.” He immediately went out to the reception hall to welcome him. After exchanging courtesies, they took their seats. Ma Teng said, “I have paid court and am about to return home, so I came to bid you farewell. Why did you refuse to see me?” Dong Cheng replied, “I was suddenly taken ill and failed to come out to welcome you. I am greatly at fault.” Ma Teng said, “Your face glows with health; I see no sign of illness.”

p.src: Dong Cheng had no answer. Ma Teng flicked his sleeves and rose at once. As he descended the steps, he sighed, “None of them are men who will save the realm!” Struck by these words, Dong Cheng held him back and asked, “Whom do you mean when you say he is no man to save the realm?” Ma Teng said, “The imperial hunt at Xutian still fills my breast with indignation; yet you are one of the Emperor’s closest kin, and still you remain sunk in wine and women, giving no thought to striking down the traitor. How can you be called a man who will rescue the imperial house from calamity?” Fearing that Ma Teng might be testing him, Dong Cheng feigned surprise and said, “Chancellor Cao is a great minister of state upon whom the court relies. Why do you speak so?” Ma Teng said furiously, “Do you still take the traitor Cao for a good man?” Dong Cheng said, “There are ears and eyes very near us. Please lower your voice.” Ma Teng said, “A craven who clings to life is not worthy to discuss great affairs!” With that, he once more made to rise. Knowing now that Ma Teng was loyal and righteous, Dong Cheng said, “Please calm your anger. Allow me to show you something.” He then invited Ma Teng into the study, brought out the edict, and showed it to him.

p.src: When Ma Teng finished reading it, his hair stood on end. He ground his teeth and bit his lips until blood filled his mouth. He said to Dong Cheng, “If you take action, I shall command the troops of Xiliang and support you from without.” Dong Cheng invited Ma Teng to meet the others, produced their covenant of loyalty, and asked him to sign his name. Ma Teng took wine, mingled it with blood, and swore an oath: “We vow to die rather than betray our pledge!” Pointing to the five men seated there, he said, “If we could find ten men, our great undertaking would succeed.” Dong Cheng said, “Men of loyalty and honor are not easily found. If we entrust ourselves to the wrong man, he will instead bring ruin upon us.” Ma Teng had them bring the register of civil and military officials and began examining it. When he reached the imperial clan of Liu, he clapped his hands and said, “Why not consult this man?” They all asked whom he meant. Unhurriedly, Ma Teng named the man. And indeed:
